questions: Does the single line loss per run still occur, and at which step and bend (start of the run, or mid-course at the sharpest bend)?
Does the 0.07 m forward offset add lag or oscillation at the controller level compared with the 0.05 m baseline?
Does steering_oscillation stay near the iteration 0 level (about 0.13 to 0.15), or does it rise?
Is the max_error still at or above 0.06 m on the slalom, and does the robot now get further along the course?

intent: Test whether a larger forward sensor offset (y = 0.07 m) improves bend anticipation and reduces the single line loss per run, using the iteration 0 geometry as the base so that only the sensor offset changes from the best-scoring design.
learning: Iterations 0 to 2 show that the best score came with the 12 mm footprint and the smallest change from the base. Changing mass, body length, footprint and span together lowered the score each time. The next race isolates sensor forward offset, so the result can be attributed to that one variable. The hypothesis is that the single line loss is a late-anticipation failure, not a coverage failure.
rationale: Iteration 2 (46.5) scored below iteration 0 (63.0) and iteration 1 (53.7). Every race ended off track with one line loss per run and max_error at 0.061 to 0.066 m. Across the three designs, the best score came from the iteration 0 geometry: 12 mm footprints, ±0.03 m sensor span, mass 0.7 kg, body_length 0.16 m, wheel_track 0.12 m. Iterations 1 and 2 each changed several things at once, and both got worse. Iteration 2 combined a 16 mm footprint, a wider span and lighter mass, and it scored lowest. The evidence therefore does not support lighter mass or wider 16 mm coverage. Mass and body changes both moved the score the wrong way, so I will not apply the Integrator's conditional move to 0.4 kg. I restore the iteration 0 geometry as the base and change one thing: the forward sensor offset, from y 0.05 to 0.07 m (the upper end of the Integrator's suggested range). The line is lost once per run, at a moment when the sensors are already at the edge of the tape, so the expected benefit is earlier reading of each bend, which lets the robot begin its turn before the wheels reach the line's edge. Expected result: line_loss_events fall below 1.0 on the s-bend and slalom, max_error stays under 0.06 m for longer, and the score rises above 63. If the score is unchanged or lower, the forward offset is not the limit, and the next test should be sensor_size 0.008 to reduce blur. Caveat: the Integrator's controller is fixed at iteration 0 gains, so any gain in this race is attributable to geometry.
